### The question for the curator

**Question 1. A local function compiled as a closure of its own class (a), or as a static method lifted out of the block (b).** Default: (a).

- **The ways.** (a): each local function of a block becomes a class of its own, made as the code generator makes a function expression's (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:3503-3567`): the variables it captures are the closure's fields, it is made when the block runs, and a call goes through its `apply`; the functions of one block see one another without a mutable cell (fork 9). (b): lambda lifting, as Scala's compiler lifts a local `def` to a private method: each local function a static method of the component's class, its captured values passed as leading parameters along every call of the group, a closure made only where the function is passed as a value, and a lifted method generic over the enclosing declaration's static parameters where its body names them.
- **What it touches of microGPT.** After the switch-over, every `for` loop over a range runs the library's recursive local `loop'` or `lop` (`Library/RangeInternals.fss:1313`, `:1328`, `:1495`, `:1515`, `:1536`, `:1560`), every `SUM` runs through `__bigOperator`'s local `body` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1317`), which is passed as a value under either way, and microGPT's `step` declares typed local functions (`explorations/run-c4/src/MicroGptFlat.fss:54-55`; `explorations/apl/mg/MicroGptApl.fss:79-81`). Under (a) a recursive split calls through the closure's `apply`, under (b) through a static method. HotSpot inlines a call at a site where it sees one receiving class as it inlines a static call, and (a) allocates one closure each time the block runs, so the planner expects no difference of speed. The two ways differ only for a local function that is called and never passed as a value: the range loops' `loop'` and `lop`, `Matrix`'s `mma` and `mm`, `Array2`'s and `Array3`'s `row` and `plane`, and microGPT's own; the five library declarations that pass a local function as a value (`__bigOperator`, `ReadableArray1`, `Matrix`'s `rmul` and `lmul`, `NaiveSeqGenerator` and `RelationalPredicateCondition`; section 4) make a closure under either way. Nothing compiles against the one library before the switch-over, so nothing can measure it now; phase 6 times microGPT compiled (PLAN, phase 6).
- **The principles.** The team's later word, its code: the code generator compiles a function value as a closure class (`forFnExpr`), and walk binds each local function as a closure in the block's environment, where the group sees itself (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/BuildLetEnvironments.java:55-81`); the team's own guard refuses local functions without a word on how (`CodeGen.java:3015-3025`, "no local functions"). The library is silent. The peers split: Scala's compiler lifts a local `def` to a method of the enclosing class; Swift's nested functions are closures over what they capture. So the principles that speak point to (a), and it is put to you for microGPT's speed alone.
- **Cost.** (a) is rung L as sized, about 0.65M. (b) threads each captured value through the group's calls and makes a lifted method generic where the block is, about 0.85M by the planner's reading. Either can be undone by one later rung of the code generator.
- **If you do not answer before the launch,** the batch runs at (a), and the question stays on your review list with the default that landed. The Fable review's judgement: the question is consequential by the test only through microGPT's compiled speed, which nothing measures before phase 6; the principles that speak to it, the team's code on both paths, point to (a); and one later rung undoes it. So it reaches you as a decision landed and then reviewed, the second of the three ways, and the launch does not wait for your answer. The review recommends (a): the code generator already makes a closure class for every function value, walk binds every local function as a closure, and five of the nine library declarations pass their local function as a value, where (b) would make a closure too.

(* A local function in a generic function reads a value of the function's type parameter, one in a method of a trait generic in a type and a size calls a method of self, and one is called from both arms of a do ... also block (functions.tex, section "Local Function Declarations"; also.tex, section "Parallel Do Expressions"). *)
component LocalFunctionGenericContextCompiled
export Executable

keep[\T extends Object\](x: T, n: ZZ32): T = do
    pick(i: ZZ32): T = if i = 0 then x else pick(i - 1) end
    pick(n)
  end

trait Hold[\E extends Object, nat n\]
    size(): ZZ32
    sumTo(k: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
        step(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = i + size()
        step(k) + step(0)
      end
end

object H3 extends Hold[\String, 3\]
    size(): ZZ32 = 3
end

bothArms(n: ZZ32): String = do
    lbl(x: ZZ32): String = (x + n).asString
    var r1: String := ""
    var r2: String := ""
    do
        r1 := lbl(1)
    also do
        r2 := lbl(2)
    end
    r1 || r2
  end

alternate[\T extends Object\](x: T, y: T, n: ZZ32): T = do
    first(i: ZZ32): T = if i = 0 then x else second(i - 1) end
    second(i: ZZ32): T = if i = 0 then y else first(i - 1) end
    first(n)
  end

splitSum(lo: ZZ32, m: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
    part(a: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): ZZ32 =
        if k = 1 then a
        else
            var left: ZZ32 := 0
            var right: ZZ32 := 0
            do
                left := part(a, k DIV 2)
            also do
                right := part(a + k DIV 2, k - k DIV 2)
            end
            left + right
        end
    part(lo, m)
  end

run(): () = do
    assert(keep[\String\]("a", 3), "a", "pick reads x of type T")
    assert(alternate[\String\]("x", "y", 3), "y", "first and second call each other and read x and y of type T")
    assert(H3.sumTo(4), 10, "step calls size of self in Hold")
    assert(bothArms(10), "1112", "lbl called from both arms")
    assert(splitSum(0, 8), 28, "part calls itself from both arms")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

content.content:
# Setting up, building, the caches, and what to rebuild

**tree**
: Checkout of the repository: the main checkout or a worktree. In a command, `<tree>` is the tree that you work in: the one that your brief names, else the one that your session starts in.

**library order**
: Five compiles that build the compiled path's library into the caches.

**DSL grammar**
: `grammar` declaration in an api, which adds syntax for a domain-specific language.

**parser directory**
: New `fortress<random>rats` folder of 5.8 MB, in which a program that imports a DSL grammar gets a Rats! parser generated when it runs. The run makes it in its JVM's temporary directory and never deletes it.

## Setting up each call

Start every Bash call with these lines. They put you at the tree's root, where this skill's commands start unless they `cd`:

    cd <tree> && mkdir -p tmp
    export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64 PATH=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin:$PATH
    export FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD FORTRESS_THREADS=1 TMPDIR=$PWD/tmp JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$PWD/tmp"
    unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS

- If `/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64` or `ant` is missing, run `apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y openjdk-25-jdk-headless ant` first.
- `bin/fortress` takes `FORTRESS_HOME` from the shell whenever it is set. If it names another tree, you run that tree's code. Check it with `echo $FORTRESS_HOME`.
- `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` is unset, because the proxy's trust-store flags in it break ant's JVM forks.

The lines give the settings of `explorations/experiment/env.sh`, with two differences:

- The JVM's temporary directory is your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
- They leave out env.sh's removal of old parser directories in `/tmp`, because your runs put theirs in your tree's `tmp/` (below).

If your brief tells you to run `source env.sh` and then to point `TMPDIR` and `JAVA_FLAGS` at `tmp/`, use the lines above. They do the same.

The library and microGPT import no DSL grammar, and of the gated tests only `ProjectFortress/syntax_abstraction_tests/ForUse.fss` does. The ungated tests beside it import one, and so do the APL experiments under `explorations/apl/`.

With the lines above, your runs that import a DSL grammar put their parser directories in `<tree>/tmp/`. Hundreds of them once filled the disk allowance. So:

- When no run of yours is live, remove yours: `rm -rf <tree>/tmp/fortress*rats`.
- Before a long run, check `df -h /`. How to read it: the `cloud-container` skill.

## Two layers of code

The repository holds two layers of code. Different tools build them, at different times, so "compile" means a different thing in each layer.

The implementation is the parser, walk, the compiled checker, the code generator and the run time. It is the Java and Scala under `ProjectFortress/src/`, with the parser grammars (`parser/*.rats`) and the syntax tree generated from `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast`. `ant compileAll` builds it into `ProjectFortress/build/` ("Building", below). `ant compile` is another name for it.

The Fortress code is the library, the tests and the programs: the `.fss` and `.fsi` files. The `fortress` commands run the phases on it and keep the results in the caches:

- Walk runs the phases on each component that a run needs. It needs no `fortress compile`.
- `fortress compile` writes a component's jar. It is for the compiled path's components only: the compiler's library, compiled tests and compiled programs.
- `fortress run` compiles no Fortress source.
- A command reuses an entry if no source that the entry depends on is newer than the entry: its own source, and the `.fsi` files of the apis that it imports, at any depth.

An edit makes stale what was built from it:

- Java or Scala: the classes in `ProjectFortress/build/`. Run `ant compileAll`. The cache entries that the edited code wrote are stale too, and no entry notices it: an entry is compared with its sources, never with the implementation. For example, after a change to a native helper's signature, its old wrapper stays in `nativewrapper_cache/`, and the run links the old signature. For this reason, the build deletes the caches when the implementation changes ("Building").
- A parser grammar: the generated parser, and every entry that it parsed. Run `ant compileAll`.
- A `.fss` or `.fsi` file of the library: the entries of that component, and after an `.fsi` edit, the entries of every component that imports the api. Walk analyses them again by itself. A component of the compiler's library needs a compile, or the library order ("After an edit of the library").
- A test or a program: its own entries. Walk and the harness analyse a walk test again by themselves. Compile a compiled test or program again, or let the harness do it.
12:Once the base build is built, run its code only as "Running the old code" says, with a private caches folder outside it. Any other run writes into the caches that every worktree is seeded from.
13-
14-## Finding or building a base build
15-
16-- If your brief names a base build, use it.
17-- If not, look in `git worktree list`. Earlier base builds are at paths such as `/home/user/fortress-base<N>`. A worktree can be your base build if it passes three checks:
18-  - `git -C <it> rev-parse HEAD` prints your base;

50-
51-If your worktree holds an edit and you need the base's behaviour, run the old code instead of reverting your edit. For example, see a test fail, or compare a program's old and new output.

53:`old-fortress.sh` runs the base build's `bin/fortress`. It sets `FORTRESS_HOME` to the base build and `FORTRESS_CACHES` to the private caches folder that you name, over your settings. Name a folder inside your worktree's `tmp/`:
54-
55:    OLD=explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh
56-    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches compile P.fss     # the compiled path ...
57-    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches run P             # ... then the run
58-    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches P.fss             # walk
59-    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches junit <worktree>/ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/X.test [Y.test ...]   # compiled .test files, in one JVM
60-
61-- Any copy of the tool works, because it runs the base build that its first argument names.

component SkLoop
export Executable

top(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = 100 x

(* a local function called from a parallel for loop, accumulating atomically *)
loopSum(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
    var acc: ZZ32 := 0
    sq(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = i i
    for i <- 1#n do atomic do acc := acc + sq(i) end end
    acc
  end

(* the block runs repeatedly: a fresh closure each time, capturing that run's k *)
rerun(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
    var total: ZZ32 := 0
    var k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < n do
        addk(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = x + k
        total := total + addk(10)
        k := k + 1
    end
    total
  end

(* a local function returning a function expression that calls a sibling *)
maker(m: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
    inc(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = x + m
    mk(): ZZ32 -> ZZ32 = fn (y: ZZ32): ZZ32 => inc(inc(y))
    g = mk()
    g(1)
  end

(* nested: an inner local function calls the outer local function recursively *)
nest(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
    outer(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
        inner(y: ZZ32): ZZ32 = if y <= 0 then 0 else 1 + outer(y - 1) end
        inner(x)
      end
    outer(n)
  end

(* two blocks of one function, each declaring h, at different types *)
twoBlocks(): String = do
    a = do
        h(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = x + 1
        h(1)
      end
    b = do
        h(s: String): String = s || "!"
        h("hi")
      end
    a.asString || b
  end

(* a local function inside a function expression's body *)
inFn(): ZZ32 = do
    f = fn (z: ZZ32): ZZ32 => do
        dbl(w: ZZ32): ZZ32 = 2 w + z
        dbl(z)
      end
    f(5)
  end

(* tuple results and unit return, io modifier, calling top-level top *)
misc(): ZZ32 = do
    var seen: ZZ32 := 0
    pair(x: ZZ32): (ZZ32, ZZ32) = (x, top(x))
    io note(x: ZZ32): () = do seen := seen + x end
    (p, q) = pair(3)
    note(p); note(q)
    seen
  end

(* a local function passed into parallel tuple arms and to a reduction *)
red(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
    cube(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = i i i
    SUM[\ZZ32\][i <- 1#n] cube(i)
  end

trait Hold[\E extends Object, nat n\]
    size(): ZZ32
    walk(k: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
        ev(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = if i = 0 then size() else od(i - 1) end
        od(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = if i = 0 then 0 - size() else ev(i - 1) end
        ev(k)
      end
end
object H5 extends Hold[\String, 5\]
    size(): ZZ32 = 5
end

topVal: ZZ32 = do
    t(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = x + 7
    t(1)
  end

run(): () = do
    println("loopSum " loopSum(10))
    println("rerun " rerun(4))
    println("maker " maker(3))
    println("nest " nest(6))
    println("twoBlocks " twoBlocks())
    println("inFn " inFn())
    println("misc " misc())
    println("red " red(4))
    println("walk " H5.walk(4) " " H5.walk(3))
    println("topVal " topVal)
  end
end
EOF
echo ok

(* A local function is called within its block, and reads a parameter, a local and a top-level value of its context (functions.tex, section "Local Function Declarations"). *)
component LocalFunctionCallCompiled
export Executable

base: ZZ32 = 100

shifted(p: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
    k: ZZ32 = 10
    add(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = x + k + p + base
    add(3) + add(4)
  end

run(): () = do
    assert(shifted(1), 229, "add reads the parameter p, the local k and the top-level base")
    m: ZZ32 = 7
    neg(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = m - x
    assert(neg(2), 5, "neg reads the local m of run")
    seven(): ZZ32 = m
    sum3(a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32, c: ZZ32): ZZ32 = a + b + c + seven()
    assert(sum3(1, 2, 3), 13, "sum3 takes three parameters and calls seven, which takes none")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

(* A local function is a value: it is passed to a higher-order function, stored by a tabulate of the program's own, and given as the value of its block (functions.tex, section "Local Function Declarations"). *)
component LocalFunctionValueCompiled
export Executable

twice(f: ZZ32 -> ZZ32, x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = f(f(x))

object Table(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> ZZ32)
    get(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = f(i)
end

tabulate(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> ZZ32): Table = Table(n, f)

adder(k: ZZ32): ZZ32 -> ZZ32 = do
    add(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = x + k
    add
  end

run(): () = do
    k: ZZ32 = 10
    add(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = x + k
    assert(twice(add, 3), 23, "add passed to twice")
    row(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = i i
    t = tabulate(4, row)
    assert(t.get(3), 9, "row stored by tabulate")
    assert(t.get(2) + t.n, 8, "the table's own n beside row")
    a5 = adder(5)
    assert(a5(1), 6, "the local add as the value of adder's block")
    assert(twice(adder(2), 1), 5, "adder's value passed on")
    mp(y: ZZ32): ZZ32 -> ZZ32 = fn (z: ZZ32): ZZ32 => add(y) + z
    assert(mp(1)(2), 13, "a function expression in mp calls its sibling add")
    outer(y: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
        inner(z: ZZ32): ZZ32 = add(z) + y
        twice(inner, 0)
      end
    assert(outer(1), 22, "inner, local to outer, calls outer's sibling add and is passed to twice")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

(* A local function calls itself, and two local functions of one block call each other, whichever is declared first (functions.tex, section "Local Function Declarations": local functions are mutually recursive). *)
component LocalFunctionRecursiveCompiled
export Executable

factorial(m: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
    fact(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = if n = 0 then 1 else n fact(n - 1) end
    fact(m)
  end

run(): () = do
    assert(factorial(5), 120, "fact calls itself")
    ev(n: ZZ32): Boolean = if n = 0 then true else od(n - 1) end
    od(n: ZZ32): Boolean = if n = 0 then false else ev(n - 1) end
    assert(ev(10), "ev(10) calls od, declared after it")
    assert(od(7), "od(7) calls ev, declared before it")
    assert(NOT ev(7), "ev(7) is false")
    step: ZZ32 = 3
    down(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = if n <= 0 then 0 else 1 + up(n - step) end
    up(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = if n <= 0 then 0 else 1 + down(n + 1) end
    assert(down(6), 5, "down and up call each other and read the local step")
    println("PASS")

# Committing and pushing

**scratch**
: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, probe programs, lists and private caches folders.

Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.

## What to commit

- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
- In a fresh clone, `.claude/worktrees/` and `.claude/agents/` show as untracked, because the lines of `.git/info/exclude` that hide them are not in the clone. Do not commit them.
- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, which is gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.

## How to commit

Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:

    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>

- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:

      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB

  If your brief gives another session line, use it.

## Pushing

Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.

- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
  3. If it lists only your commits, push the three refs with this one command, and wait for it to end:

         git push --atomic origin main main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8 main:blinded-fable

     With `--atomic`, the three refs update together or not at all. Do not pipe the command into another command, since a pipe hides a refusal. A refusal shows as a line that starts with `!`, and as a non-zero exit. The last ref keeps `blinded-fable` current. If the container is lost, the platform rebuilds it from that branch.
- Push no branch that this section does not name, unless your brief names it.
- If a push is refused, push nothing more, and do not run it again. Report the refused ref and git's message.
